details:
Dear VRChat Team,

I am a long‑time VRChat user from Taiwan, and I am writing to kindly request that you add “Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien)” as a selectable language in your language settings.

In recent updates, VRChat has significantly expanded its localization support, adding many interface languages and even distinguishing several Sinitic languages such as Cantonese, Teochew, and Mandarin in its language‑related options. This clearly shows VRChat’s strong commitment to accessibility for Chinese‑speaking communities worldwide and to serving a truly global, multilingual user base.

I would like to present a few reasons why adding Taiwanese as a separate language option would be beneficial both for users and for VRChat:

1. A large and active Taiwanese user base

Taiwan has a very active VR and gaming community, and VRChat is particularly popular among younger users who enjoy socializing and creating content in virtual worlds.

For many of us, Taiwanese is not just a “dialect” of Chinese, but a living everyday language used at home, with friends, and in cultural and creative works. Recognizing Taiwanese in VRChat’s language options would greatly increase the sense of inclusion and belonging for Taiwanese players.

2. Cultural identity and representation

Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien) has its own rich oral tradition, music, comedy, and online culture, and it plays a central role in Taiwanese identity.

International standards such as ISO 639‑3 already classify Southern Min with the code “nan,” and there have been specific proposals and discussions around recognizing Taiwanese within this framework, highlighting its distinct identity and literature.

By listing “Taiwanese (Taiwanese Hokkien)” as its own language option (for example, “Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien)” mapped internally to nan or an appropriate tag), VRChat would be aligning with this direction and acknowledging a unique linguistic and cultural community.

3. Consistency with multilingual support trends in tech

Many large projects and platforms are actively extending support to regional languages and varieties that have strong user communities, as seen in crowdsourced speech datasets and language technology projects for Taiwanese Minnan.

VRChat has already shown that it values community‑driven localization and allows contributors to refine translations through official channels like Discord‑based localization workflows. Adding Taiwanese as a language slot would allow volunteers and native speakers to help you maintain and improve this localization in a sustainable way.

4. Practical implementation suggestions

Language name in menu: “Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien)” to make it understandable both to international users and to locals.

Technical tagging: internally, you could leverage existing standards such as ISO 639‑3 “nan” for Southern Min, possibly combined with region/script subtags if needed, as already discussed in web and standards communities.

Community support: many Taiwanese users, including myself, would be happy to participate via your existing localization suggestion process (e.g., joining the official Discord and following your per‑language guidelines) to help provide accurate and natural translations.

From a user perspective, seeing Taiwanese listed alongside other languages already supported in VRChat would send a strong positive message about inclusivity, cultural respect, and your commitment to representing real communities in the metaverse. It would also make it easier for new users in Taiwan—especially those less comfortable with English or Mandarin—to understand the UI, settings, safety features, and community guidelines in the language they use most naturally.

Thank you very much for taking the time to read this request. I deeply appreciate all the work your team has done to improve localization and accessibility so far, and I hope you will consider adding “Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien)” as an official language option in a future update. If you need any feedback, user testing, or community coordination from Taiwanese users, I would be glad to help.

Sincerely,

VRChat Username: RyuDensetsu

Location: Taiwan
title: Request to Add “Taiwanese (台語 / Taiwanese Hokkien)” as a Language Option in VRChat
